figures.finding: Namibia taxes an individual's Namibian-source income at progressive rates: nothing to N$100,000, 18% to N$150,000, then 25%, 28%, 30%, 32%, and 37% above N$1,550,000.
figures.applies: Tax year 1 March 2026 to 28 February 2027 (Deloitte 2026). Source basis: residents and non-residents alike.

sources.said: Individuals are taxable on all income received or accrued from a Namibian source or a deemed Namibian source.
Any person who earns a salary of more than N$ 100,000 per annum should register as a taxpayer

figures.finding: Social security is 1.8% of basic salary, 0.9% each from employee and employer, at most N$99 each a month (on earnings above N$11,000).

sources.said: Social security contributions are calculated at 1.8% of the employee’s basic salary, shared equally between the employer and the employee (0.9% each). The current maximum contribution is NAD 198 per employee (i.e., NAD 99 payable by the employee and NAD 99 payable by the employer) for employees whose monthly earnings are above NAD 11,000.

figures.finding: The employer withholds PAYE monthly at the individual rates and remits it monthly.

sources.said: Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer under the PAYE system and remitted monthly to the tax authorities.

figures.finding: Payments to non-resident entertainers bear a 10% withholding tax unless a treaty reduces it; non-residents otherwise pay the same rates on Namibian employment and business income.
figures.applies: Whether the 10% is final was not stated.

sources.said: A 10% withholding tax applies to payments made to nonresident entertainers
The same tax rates apply to nonresidents in respect of employment and business income earned in Namibia.

figures.finding: VAT is 15%; a business must register above an annual turnover of N$1 million.

sources.said: The registration threshold for VAT purposes is annual turnover of NAD 1 million.

figures.finding: The tax year runs 1 March to 28 February; returns are due by 30 June for salaried and 30 September for other individuals.
figures.applies: Due dates fall in the calendar year the tax year ends.

sources.said: The tax year for individuals is from 1 March to 28 February.
Returns are due by 30 June for salaried individuals, and by 30 September for non-salaried individuals.
